sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Three more warnings show the rich comparison card instead of a sentence only. "Live title date uses "-"" (release and release group titles, event names, recording comments): the text over the same text with "‐" in its date, only the date's hyphens marked — a hyphen in the venue stays. "Extra title information starts uppercase": the title over the same title with its keywords in lower case, "(Live in Asbury Park 2009)" over "(live in Asbury Park 2009)". "Title truncated with "…"": the title in one row with the "…" marked, since the full title is not on the page. The cards also show in the note box above a link preview.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: MusicBrainz pages: "Aa Check title style (MB guidelines)" at the top of the ⚠️ WARNING menu checks every title on the page against the MusicBrainz style guide and adds five warnings: "Title not in MB title case" ("Prayer For The Weary" → "Prayer for the Weary"), "ASCII punctuation in title" ("Don't" → "Don’t", " - " → " – ", "..." → "…"), "Series number without comma" ("Broadcasts Vol. 5" → "Broadcasts, Vol. 5"), "Featured artist in title" and "Extra title information to remove" ("(bonus track)", "[… Cover]"). Each filters the page from the menu and from the column's 📊 Findings - Warning section, and the hover card shows the title over its MusicBrainz style with only what differs marked. Only certain cases are flagged: titles in another language or in sentence case, live bootleg titles, phrasal "Take On Me", "& The E Street Band", lower-case words in "(…)" and anything in "[…]" are left alone.

The check runs only when asked for, since it costs about 0.2 s per 10,000 different titles; it then stays on for the page until a reload, and the menu row shows how many titles it checked and how long that took. ⚙️ Settings → ⚠️ Findings → "Check title style automatically" (off by default) runs it on every load; each of the five warnings and their tint have their own switches there. The WARNING menu now shows on every MusicBrainz page with titles, to offer the check.
